## Per episode

- **#47 Queen Jinduk.** Cut the accession quote, which called Seungman Sunduk’s *younger sister* (the decision is cousin). Built a climax around Heewon’s lines, kept verbatim. Yushin’s hand stays on his sword belt, and Jinduk tells him to let go. A runner brings word that Baekje has taken three forts. Jinduk can’t dream it the way her cousin did. Yushin wants to go; Chunchu wants “a bigger door”. She sends both, and it rains, unpredicted. That rain is the maids’ coronation.
- **#48 Huangdi.** Cut the record that gave away the emperor’s yes (*Taizong deeply agreed, and promised to send an army*). The yes now arrives only in the Six Steeds gallery and through the poem. Also cut:
  - every chengyu card whose line already glosses the idiom;
  - the tribute, department, exam and military diagrams;
  - the Qin flashback;
  - two horse speeches;
  - Wu’s banquet catechism and the Gija/Wiman flashback;
  - the On Gunhae record and the modern banner gag.
  Added a beat to plant Jukji and On Gunhae as the tenth and eleventh heads in the ward count. It pays off when Chunchu lands home: “Nine… He never asked me for anything either.” Also added a line about the army: *Chunchu has asked for it three ways…* The Wu hallway, the dying-emperor lines and the Six Steeds stay intact. They hold ~60 stills, which is why the episode is still ~4,700 words, over the 4,000 cap. A further cut means retiring stills, which is Heewon’s call.
- **#49 Royal Secretariat.** The rewind is now motivated: the promise-maker has been dead two years, and the card sends us back to his deathbed. Changes:
  - Diagrams, three quotes and the Gaozong edict are out.
  - The lame-duck Council paragraph became an Alchun scene (*That’s a very polite way of saying a chair*).
  - Jinduk weaves the ode herself.
  - New Sabi scene: Euija reads the emperor’s letter aloud (“Heaven just counted my enemies for me. One!”) and Gyebek answers “For now, one.”
  - Fixed the untranslated 중시 and removed Naniwa/Tsukushi and the AD year.
- **#50 Jiabeng.** Opens on the announced rewind. Taizong’s last order is the purple horse nearest the door, which pays off #48. Cut three quotes, the temple-name decree and the duplicate Sabi beat; Sabi is now in #49.
- **#51 King Muyeol.** The election is a scene now. The room offers the chair to Alchun first. He refuses with the Samguk Sagi words in his own mouth (quote block cut) and calls back his #44 “chair” line. Removed the emoji speakers. The “private grudge” line is now Alchun’s; it was Yushin with the 🙎 label, and Yushin’s own reaction follows it. Cut the bone-rank quote (#53 explains it) and the Wu monologue. Added a Jahee beat (“You carried a one”) that sets up #52.
- **#52 Jahee.** The flashback is announced (“Ten years earlier”). A new obstacle: Yushin orders the grain out on the morning tide, and the books are forty sacks short. The two count all night, and the kiss is kept. Climax: Bupmin finds the sacks, misses the tide, and Yushin hits him once and feeds the company. The coda returns to the coronation year: the Tang-silk court, the new era, the plan to unite Samhan, the six old houses muttering (“Now he comes out of a Secretariat”), and Alchun’s “ask how the first one got here”.
- **#53 Hyukgose.** Removed “Old Joseon”; the northern kingdom is unnamed and called “another story”. Cut three quotes, the manifesto narration and the clan table. Changes:
  - The manifesto is now Alpyung’s speech, interrupted by Alyoung: “Who measures the virtue?”
  - Gourd → Park.
  - The Sacred/True Bone explanation is in narration.
  - The Six Elders payoff is in a coronation-yard coda. Alchun: “When Bidam said he was Six-Elder blood, he meant he was here before the egg.” Bupmin: “He also said there was no Kim.” Alchun: “There wasn’t. Not that morning.” Chunchu’s line leads to #54.
- **#54 Talhae.** Glossed Wa and cut three quotes. Added a coda: Muyeol can’t sleep in the stolen house. Munhee: “If a rooster crows, it’s a rooster.”
- **#55 Alji.** The new opener pays off Bidam’s line. Cut two quotes. Added a middle scene: Talhae offers Alji the chair, and Alji says “Gold doesn’t rust.” Added a Gyerim coda: Chunchu tells Bupmin why bones are counted (“every house that ever wore this crown arrived in something”), then turns to Baekje. The card leads to #56 Exile.

- #48 is over 4,000 words (see above).
